question_text: $0.10\text{ mole}$ of a carbohydrate with empirical formula $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$ contains $1\text{ g}$ of hydrogen. Its molecular formula will be:
explanation: Moles of H atoms = $1\text{ g} / 1\text{ g/mol} = 1\text{ mol}$. In $0.10\text{ mol}$ of carbohydrate, total moles of H = $1$, so per mole of carbohydrate there are $10$ H atoms, giving $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5$.

question_text: The reduction product of Citral with $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{Alcohol}$ is:
explanation: Reduction of the aldehyde group in citral using sodium amalgam and alcohol yields geraniol.

question_text: Arrange the following nucleophiles in the decreasing order of their nucleophilicity: $\text{NH}_2^-, \text{NH}_3, \text{C}_2\text{H}_5-\text{NH}_2, \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{NH}_2$
explanation: Negative charge makes $\text{NH}_2^-$ the strongest. Ethylamine is more basic than ammonia due to $+I$ effect, and aniline is least basic due to resonance delocalization.

question_text: $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism operates in the hydrolysis of:
explanation: Tertiary alkyl halides like t-butyl chloride undergo hydrolysis predominantly via stable carbocation formation in an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway.

question_text: Iodoform cannot be prepared from:
explanation: Iodoform test requires a methyl ketone or a secondary/primary alcohol containing the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})-$ group (like ethanol, acetaldehyde, isopropanol). Methanol lacks this grouping.

question_text: Isobutane upon bromination under the influence of ultraviolet light at 127 °C affords the following major product:
explanation: Bromination is highly regioselective for tertiary hydrogens due to the stability of tertiary free radicals, forming tert-butyl bromide as the major product.

question_text: Identify the functional groups from the below mentioned options that lead to weakening of benzoic acid: A. -OH, B. -Cl, C. -NH2, D. -NO2
explanation: Electron-donating groups like -OH and -NH2 via resonance increase electron density on the ring, destabilizing the benzoate anion and thus decreasing/weakening the acidity of benzoic acid.

question_text: Phenol upon treatment with bromine in the presence of carbondisulphide at 0 °C yields:
explanation: In non-polar solvents like CS2 at low temperatures, phenol undergoes monobromination predominantly yielding the para-isomer (4-bromophenol) as the major product.

question_text: In the determination of configuration of glucose, Fischer subjected (-) arabinose to Ruff's degradation. The four-carbon sugar obtained by the degradation process was:
explanation: Ruff degradation of (-) arabinose shortens the carbon chain by one carbon atom, yielding (-) erythrose.

question_text: Insertion of a oxygen in a carbonyl compound to form an ester is known as:
explanation: The Baeyer-Villiger oxidation is an organic reaction that oxidizes a ketone to an ester by inserting an oxygen atom adjacent to the carbonyl group.

question_text: Controlled alkylation of a ketone via an enamine intermediate is named as:
explanation: The Stork enamine alkylation is a chemical reaction used to alkylate ketones or aldehydes via an enamine intermediate.

question_text: Among the following organic compounds, the one that is non-aromatic is: [Diagram representing cyclic hydrocarbon rings with varying electron and charge patterns]
explanation: Cyclopentadienyl anion is aromatic (6 pi electrons), whereas non-aromatic cyclic systems lack continuous cyclic conjugation or planarity.

question_text: The major product formed in the above reaction (Diels-Alder cycloaddition) is:
explanation: Diels-Alder reaction of furan and maleic anhydride typically yields the endo-adduct as the major kinetic product.

question_text: The major product formed in the above acid-catalyzed reaction is:
explanation: Acid-catalyzed condensation/substitution yields the corresponding stable anilide derivative.

question_text: The set of specific reagents used in the above-mentioned synthesis of m-(n-Butyl)toluene from n-propyl m-tolyl ketone is:
explanation: The Wolff-Kishner reduction (using hydrazine and base like NaOH) reduces the ketone carbonyl to a methylene group.

question_text: The major product formed in the above-given Knorr synthesis is:
explanation: Knorr pyrrole synthesis involves the reaction of an alpha-amino ketone with an active methylene compound to yield substituted pyrroles.

question_text: Arrange the following Lowry-Bronsted acids into their decreasing order of acidity (highest to lowest) [P] $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ [Q] $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$ [R] $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ [S] $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$
explanation: Acidity order of conjugate acids: $\text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{RC}\equiv\text{CH} > \text{ROH} > \text{RNH}_2$. Thus $\text{H}_2\text{O} (R) > \text{propyne} (Q) > \text{ethanol} (P) > \text{methylamine} (S)$.

question_text: Alkenes show typical electrophilic addition reactions. If an electron withdrawing group is attached to one of the carbons bearing the double bond, what will happen to the mechanism of the addition reaction
explanation: Strong electron-withdrawing groups on an alkene deplete electron density, shifting the pathway toward nucleophilic addition reactions.

question_text: Aprotic polar solvents increase the rate of SN2 reactions manifold. Enhancement in the rate of such reactions is due to which one of the following effects

options.A: Solvation of the anion by the solvent leaving the cation unaffected
options.B: Solvation of both of the ionic species
options.C: Desolvation of the cation and solvation of the anion
options.D: Solvation of the cation by the solvent leaving the anion unaffected

explanation: Polar aprotic solvents selectively solvate cations while leaving nucleophilic anions bare (unsolvated), greatly enhancing their nucleophilicity in SN2 reactions.

question_text: Five-membered heteroaromatic compounds show a much higher rate of electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions than the six-membered ones. This is due to which one of the following reasons?

options.A: Five-membered heteroaromatic compounds have higher circulating electron density in the ring than the six-membered ones
options.B: Five-membered heteroaromatic compounds have lower circulating electron density in the ring than the six-membered ones
options.C: Five-membered rings are smaller in size than the six membered ones which affects their reaction rates
options.D: Six membered heteroaromatic rings are flat while the five-membered ones are puckered

explanation: Five-membered heteroaromatic rings have 6 $\pi$ electrons distributed over 5 atoms, giving them a higher electron density per carbon compared to six-membered rings.

question_text: Pyridine is more basic than pyrrole. This is due to which of the following facts

options.A: Lone pair of electrons on N in pyrrole is localized
options.B: Lone pair of electrons on N in pyridine is localized
options.C: Nitrogen of pyrrole has one hydrogen atom attached to it while pyridine does not haveany
options.D: Pyridine has three double bonds while pyrrole has only two

explanation: In pyridine, the nitrogen lone pair resides in an $sp^2$ orbital perpendicular to the aromatic $\pi$ system and is localized (available for protonation), whereas pyrrole's lone pair is part of the aromatic sextet.
